transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-08-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Valdez (Redwood SE), Elena Rojas (Solis - Head of Platform), Tariq Malik (Solis - SRE Lead), Pooja Shah (Solis - Director ML Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, imperfect):
Solis is evaluating Redwood for a hybrid deployment; primary concerns are VPC/private control plane, gateway/proxy pattern integration with their API gateway, SDK examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex, and rate limit/quotas behavior under bursty traffic. They want to run a short pilot on Dedicated capacity then evaluate Private on prem later. Next steps: send architecture docs, quickstart repo, schedule perf deep-dive.

Topics: VPC/private control plane, proxy/gateway pattern, SDK + LangChain/LlamaIndex integration, rate limiting and quotas, observability/tracing hooks, KV cache behavior, rollout strategy (canary).

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE. Marcus, our SE, is with me. How are you all?
[00:07] Elena Rojas: Good, thanks. Sorry for the slightly late start, had a stack rotation.
[00:11] Marcus Valdez: No worries. Should be a quickish intro and then we can dig into the proxy and VPC bits.
[00:17] Tariq Malik: Cool. For context, we're running a custom API gateway into our internal mesh, using Envoy and some homegrown auth. We want to evaluate three modes: start with Hosted for quick dev, move to Dedicated for predictable throughput, and eventually Private in our VPC. The big question is how the gateway integrates and whether we can keep traffic inside our network.
[00:36] Avery Chen: Great, that aligns with what we've seen. Marcus, want to run through the options quickly?
[00:40] Marcus Valdez: Sure. So Hosted gives you fastest time-to-value — you call our API, it hits our control plane. Dedicated reserves GPU pools for you, predictable throughput, and you can add a VPC peering option so traffic can stay within a region. Private basically gives you a customer-managed control plane that runs in your VPC or on-prem.
[01:01] Pooja Shah: When you say VPC peering for Dedicated, is that egress through Redwood or are we establishing direct network tunnels? We are strict about no data egress without encryption and audit.
[01:11] Marcus Valdez: With Dedicated we offer a private link/peering option plus mTLS and explicit flow controls. For Private you control the plane, so logs and KV cache never leave your network. There are also KMS integrations.
[01:23] Elena Rojas: Okay. On the integration side we use LangChain heavily, and some teams use LlamaIndex for retrieval. We want to know if you have first-class SDKs or sample connectors.
[01:33] Avery Chen: Yes — we have SDKs in Python, Node, and some community examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. I'll drop the quickstart repo link after the call. The LangChain examples show how to swap the Redwood Client into the LLM chain and how to use our streaming interface.
[01:46] Tariq Malik: Are those examples compatible with our gateway pattern? Right now our requests go through an internal proxy that handles tenant headers and rate limiting. We can't change that easily.
[01:56] Marcus Valdez: That's a common setup. We often recommend a sidecar or edge-proxy pattern where the gateway forwards calls to Redwood and injects tenant metadata. There's a sample middleware in the SDK that shows header forwarding and signature validation. The proxy can also do client-side batching if you want to aggregate small requests.
[02:14] Pooja Shah: Signature validation, is that HMAC? We're using SAML for SSO and KMS for keys.
[02:20] Marcus Valdez: We support signed tokens, HMAC, and also SAML-based SSO for the console. For private keys you can configure your KMS/HSM, yes.
[02:26] Elena Rojas: Can you speak to rate limits? We have bursts from our mobile app at 500 req/s for short windows. If we go Hosted initially is there a sandboxing behavior where the request is queued or throttled? We can't have silent 429s for user-visible flows.
[02:40] Avery Chen: Good question. We have quota and tiering. For Hosted we enforce per-account quotas which return 429 and a Retry-After header. For production flows we usually move to Dedicated where you get reserved throughput; Dedicated supports burst policies and can integrate with your gateway to surface backpressure upstream. Private you control the quota logic entirely.
[02:59] Tariq Malik: The Retry-After header won't cut it for some flows. We want deterministic backpressure. Is there API-level streamable feedback or websockets that can signal throttling gracefully?
[03:10] Marcus Valdez: We support streaming responses for generation and also have a 'preflight' token check API that your gateway can call to reserve capacity. There's also a gRPC path in Dedicated/Private for lower overhead and more signal semantics — that's what customers with strict p95 goals use.
[03:25] Elena Rojas: Marcus, you mentioned KV cache earlier in the docs — can you explain what that means for us? Our LLM calls are relatively short but some chains rely on prefix caching.
[03:34] Marcus Valdez: Sure. Our runtime exposes an optional KV cache for prefix tokens and retrieval results; it saves repeated computation for repeated context. For Private/Dedicated you can tune cache TTLs, and in Private the cache can be pinned to a local store so it doesn't hit our network. In Hosted the cache is managed by Redwood and expires based on usage.
[03:50] Pooja Shah: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex? Does vector storage need to be colocated? We currently use an internal vector DB — Qdrant.
[03:58] Marcus Valdez: LlamaIndex typically points at your vector store. Our SDK examples show connectors for Qdrant and Pinecone. For latency-sensitive retrieval you want the vector DB in the same VPC/region as the inference endpoint — with Private you can ensure that. 
[04:14] Elena Rojas: Observability: what telemetry do you expose? We need token-level cost breakdowns, traces tied to spans in our distributed tracing (we use Jaeger), and audit logs for every request.
[04:24] Marcus Valdez: Console has per-token cost and latency breakdowns, and we emit OpenTelemetry spans you can ingest to your tracing backend. Audit logs are available and can be shipped to your S3 or via syslog for Private/Dedicated. Hosted also has audit, but for retention beyond X days it's an add-on.
[04:41] Tariq Malik: Okay that helps. On rollout strategy, we want to canary on a small tenant slice and then ramp. Can Redwood handle per-tenant model variants and fallback?
[04:51] Avery Chen: Yes — our routing supports policy-based routing by tenant, latency targets, and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants if the primary model isn't available. The console lets you configure canaries and A/B experiments.
[05:02] Elena Rojas: Good. I want to touch on security review items — SOC2, ISO, breach notifications, and the encryption of logs in transit and at rest. We will have our security team review your docs.
[05:12] Marcus Valdez: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO-27001 attestations, and we provide SOC artifacts via an NDA. Logs are encrypted TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest; for Private you can plug in your own KMS so keys never leave your control.
[05:25] Pooja Shah: Can we get a spreadsheet of typical token unit economics so our finance folks can model costs for 10M tokens/month?
[05:32] Avery Chen: Absolutely — I'll attach the pricing worksheet and an example cost model.
[05:35] Tariq Malik: One practical question — our gateway is doing per-tenant rate limit counting. If Redwood enforces its own quotas upstream we need deterministic counting so the gateway and Redwood don't have conflicting views. Any recommendations?
[05:47] Marcus Valdez: Best practice is to have the gateway be the source of truth for short-lived counters and use Redwood's quota as a higher-level safety net. We support a 'quota reservation' call so the gateway can ask to reserve N tokens for a batch. That way the gateway can change the behaviour depending on the response.
[06:03] Elena Rojas: Does that reservation call add much latency? We're sensitive at p95.
[06:08] Marcus Valdez: If you use gRPC in Dedicated/Private it's sub-ms; for REST it adds a round-trip but you can batch reservations. We'll demonstrate in the deep-dive.
[06:17] Pooja Shah: Regarding SDKs, are there patterns for chaining LLM calls (complex chains) without repeatedly paying for the same context? For example, multiple refine steps.
[06:26] Marcus Valdez: You can use the KV cache + streaming tokens to reduce costs. Also we have a 'session' abstraction that keeps a warm KV cache and reuses it across related calls in a session ID. That's in the SDK examples — Marcus to highlight the snippet.
[06:39] Avery Chen: Quick note — we'll share a LangChain notebook that shows the session pattern and a LlamaIndex connector example that points to Qdrant.
[06:46] Tariq Malik: Sounds good. I'd like to schedule the perf sim mentioned earlier — Pooja can share payload distribution and we'll iterate.
[06:54] Pooja Shah: I'll send a sample trace and payload histogram. We are roughly 70% short queries (<64 tokens) and 30% long chains. P95 target is 120ms for small queries.
[07:07] Marcus Valdez: Noted. We'll attempt to replicate and advise on batching thresholds and quantization profiles — sometimes switching to a 4-bit quantized variant reduces cost at minimal quality loss.
[07:19] Elena Rojas: Any gotchas with streaming when behind our proxy? We use HTTP/2 for streaming internally.
[07:25] Marcus Valdez: Streaming over HTTP/2 works; the sample middleware in the SDK shows chunked streaming and reassembly. If your proxy terminates streams you may want to tunnel the stream to the client or do server-side aggregation.
[07:39] Short pause / background chatter
[07:45] Avery Chen: Okay let's recap and call out next steps.
[07:48] Avery Chen: Action items: I'll share Private architecture doc, VPC checklist, pricing worksheet, and the LangChain/LlamaIndex quickstart repo. Marcus will run a 1k concurrent simulation and prepare perf notes for the deep-dive. Pooja will provide payload distribution and p95 targets. We'll schedule the 60-minute perf deep-dive for 2027-08-10 with Marcus and Tariq.
[08:08] Elena Rojas: That works. One more ask — can you provide an example syslog/audit payload so our security team can map fields?
[08:15] Marcus Valdez: Yes, we'll include a sample audit log schema and an example.
[08:20] Tariq Malik: Thanks. Do you have any docs on onboarding timelines for Dedicated vs Private?
[08:25] Avery Chen: Dedicated typically 2-4 weeks for reserved pools + network setup, Private depending on infra can be 4-8+ weeks. We'll include a timeline doc.
[08:33] Elena Rojas: Great. Thanks everyone.
[08:35] Call end.
